claim.claim-text: 1. A nerve growth factor fusion protein, represented by a general formula A-B or A-L-B, wherein A is a human nerve growth factor, L is a linker peptide, and B is a mutant of an Fc moiety of IgG1, or a fragment of the Fc moiety of IgG1, and wherein the mutant of the Fc moiety comprises a site mutation associated with antibody dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC)/complement dependent cytotoxicity (CDC) activity, or a deglycosylation mutation.

2. The nerve growth factor fusion protein according to claim 1, wherein the human nerve growth factor is a wild-type human nerve growth factor, or the human nerve growth factor comprising F12E, K32G, K32L, K32Y, R59L, R59A, D65A, D65G, K74L, K88F, K88L, K88E, K88G, Q96E, R114V, R114F, R114G, R114L, or F101A reference to the amino acid position set forth in the wild-type human nerve growth factor.

3. The nerve growth factor fusion protein according to claim 1 or 2, wherein the human nerve growth factor has an amino acid sequence of any one of SEQ ID No: 1, SEQ ID No: 2, and SEQ ID No: 13 to SEQ ID No: 30 in the sequence listing.

4. The nerve growth factor fusion protein according to claims 1 to 3, wherein the human nerve growth factor comprising F12E reference to the amino acid position set forth in the wild-type human nerve growth factor.

5. The nerve growth factor fusion protein according to any one of claims 1 to 4, wherein the mutant of the Fc moiety of IgG1 has an amino acid sequence of SEQ ID No: 7, or an amino acid sequence of SEQ ID No: 7 with the first 5 amino acids deleting at N-terminal.

6. The nerve growth factor fusion protein according to any one of claims 1 to 5, wherein L is a glycine-rich peptide or a peptide having a sequence [Gly-Gly-Gly-Gly-Ser]n, wherein n is 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6, preferably n is 2-6, more preferably n is 3-4, and most preferably n is 3.

7. The nerve growth factor fusion protein according to any one of claims 1 to 6, wherein L is not more than 30 amino acids in length; preferably not more than 20 amino acids in length, and more preferably not more than 15 amino acids in length.
8. The nerve growth factor fusion protein according to any one of claims 1 to 7, wherein the nerve growth factor fusion protein has an amino acid sequence of SEQ ID No: 10.
9. A polynucleotide sequence, encoding the nerve growth factor fusion protein according to any one of claims 1 to 8.

10. An expression vector, comprising the nucleotide sequence according to claim 9; preferably, the expression vector is a DNA vector or a viral vector; and more preferably, the DNA vector is selected from the group consisting of a DNA plasmid vector, a liposome bound thereto, and a polymer bound thereto; and preferably, the DNA plasmid vector is a eukaryotic expression vector; and the viral vector is selected from the group consisting of an adeno-associated virus vector, a lentiviral vector and an adenoviral vector.
11. A method for preparing a nerve growth factor fusion protein, comprising:

transforming the expression vector according to claim 10 into a host cell, and culturing a resultant recombinant cell to express the expression vector, so as to obtain the nerve growth factor fusion protein.

12. A host cell, comprising the expression vector according to claim 10; and preferably, the host cell is a mammalian cell, preferably a Chinese hamster ovary cell, a human embryonic kidney 293 cell, a COS cell or a Hela cell.

13. A pharmaceutical composition, comprising a pharmaceutically acceptable excipient, and one or more of the nerve growth factor fusion protein according to any one of claims 1 to 8, the polynucleotide sequence according to claim 9, the expression vector according to claim 10 and the host cell according to claim 12; preferably, the pharmaceutical composition is an injection, a capsule, a tablet or powder; and more preferably, the pharmaceutical composition is an injection comprising a pharmaceutically acceptable excipient and a nerve growth factor fusion protein.

14. The nerve growth factor fusion protein according to any one of claims 1 to 8 for use in treating a nervous system disease, wherein the nervous system disease is selected from Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease, stroke, ALS, peripheral neuropathy, and a neuropathy associated with diabetes, AIDS or chemotherapy.
15. The nerve growth factor fusion protein according to any one of claims 1 to 8 for use in effectively reducing weight.
